feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence: iteration 10 (kd 0.75) scored 700.7, the best observed, with the oval at 20/20 and s-bend at 20/20 (line-loss 0.55). Iteration 9 (kd 0.6) scored 669.8 and iteration 8 (kd 0.45, kp 3.0) scored 610.7, so the controller gain produced the sharp-track gains on your geometry. Your iteration 11 geometry matches the iteration 9 and 10 values, so I have held it unchanged and set only the controller to the iteration 10 gains. Your geometry choices from iterations 2 to 7 (span, footprint, forward position, wheel_track, mass) have each been tested, and none moved the sharp tracks beyond what the controller change did. Decision rules: since no further iteration follows, the only thing that can change is what the unseen track reveals in the final race. Keep the geometry as written. Do not attempt a wider span or narrower wheel_track now, since the evidence from iterations 2, 3 and 5 to 6 says those changes hurt or were flat.
requested_changes: Hold the iteration 11 geometry exactly: wheel_track 0.09 m, sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 m in 0.015 m steps with y = 0.07 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, mass 0.5 kg, body 0.12 x 0.16 m. Evidence: iteration 9 (669.8) and iteration 10 (700.7) both used these values, and geometry tests since iteration 4 have been flat or negative on the sharp tracks.

Do not change sensor y, span, footprint or wheel_track for the final race. Evidence: y 0.06 to 0.07 m helped only the oval (iteration 4), span 0.04 m hurt every track (iteration 2), footprint 0.016 m hurt the oval (iteration 3), and wheel_track 0.09 m is the floor reached in iteration 6.

Keep mass at 0.5 kg unless the controller is changed. Evidence: mass 0.7 to 0.5 kg lifted s-bend finishes from 0/20 to 2/20 under the old gains (iterations 6 and 7), and the 0.5 kg body held oscillation at 0.21 to 0.22 under kd 0.6 to 0.75 (iterations 9 and 10).
